sources.title: Historical Basemaps: Taiwan after 1945 index and geometry
sources.note: Local index, five decoded snapshots and point tests in identities.json and geometry-checks.json. Main-island geometry omits offshore islands; Hualien point outside 1994 outline.

sources.title: National Human Rights Museum: White Terror Period
sources.note: Direct institutional background and dated chronology: 1945 takeover, 1949 relocation and martial law, 1987 lifting in Taiwan and Penghu, 1992 Kinmen and Matsu military administration endpoint.

sources.title: Congressional Research Service: Taiwan, Background and U.S. Relations, 15 August 2025
sources.note: Direct official report, introduction, historical background and democratization. Available official HTML version dated 15 August 2025; no claim to have read a later 2026 edition. All IF 10275 versions treated as one work for reuse.

sources.title: Ministry of Culture: Our 2.28, 70 Years After the 2.28 Incident, 2017
sources.note: Indexed original National Museum of Taiwan History exhibition announcement, 2017; documents, relics and community memory of February 1947.

sources.title: National Human Rights Museum: Green Island White Terror Memorial Park
sources.note: Direct overview, New Life Correction Center, Oasis Villa and surviving prison layout. Museum models/wax figures are modern interpretation, not excavated contemporary objects.

sources.title: Presidential Office: Presidents of the Republic of China
sources.note: Indexed original Chinese museum/interpretation page, Chiang Ching-kuo section: lifting martial law and opening visits to mainland relatives in 1987.

sources.title: ITRI Today, Fall 2023: The Birth of Taiwan’s Semiconductor Industry
sources.note: Direct institutional retrospective and indexed original. 1976 RCA agreement, nineteen engineers and divided training specialisms; 1987 TSMC spin-off of facilities, technologies and 98 professionals.

sources.title: Ministry of Education: Education in Taiwan, 2022/2023
sources.note: Full indexed original selected sections, educational system and preschool/compulsory education, printed pages 20 to 21. Distinguishes nine compulsory years from twelve-year basic education.

sources.title: Taipei Indigenous Peoples Commission: 2024 first-term holiday preschool course exhibition announcement
sources.note: Full indexed original Chinese announcement; course ran 9 March to 29 June 2024, ages three to six in Nangang. Siraya and Taokas included; proposed 30 June display and family activities are not treated as independently observed outcomes.

sources.title: National Health Insurance Administration: Development of the Healthcare System in Taiwan
sources.note: Direct official institutional timeline: thirteen previous employment-based schemes, launch on 1 March 1995, smart card from 1 January 2004.

sources.title: Taiwan Epidemiology Bulletin: Expansion of Hepatitis B Immunization Program, 1986, volume 2 number 8
sources.note: Full indexed original abstract, 1 July 1984 launch; initial program targeted infants of infected mothers and screened pregnant women. Historical program details, not medical instructions.

sources.title: Environmental Management Administration: New Restroom Culture
sources.note: Full indexed original, checked 23 September 2026. Explicitly cites 12 August 2025 guidelines, dispersible toilet paper standard CNS 1091, items not to flush, and sitting/squatting toilet options. Direct refetch timed out; indexed text used.

sources.title: Ministry of Culture: Garbage trucks may sing a different tune in Taoyuan, 18 November 2016
sources.note: Full indexed original government account: familiar classical melodies and proposed Hakka music in Longtan; approval is not proof every truck changed immediately.

sources.title: Taipei tourism authority: Raohe Street Tourist Night Market
sources.note: Indexed original bilingual entry, checked 23 September 2026, listed specialties and Songshan location; no claim about every household’s diet.

sources.title: Executive Yuan: Promulgation of same-sex marriage law, 22 May 2019
sources.note: Full indexed original announcement: law passed 17 May, promulgated 22 May, effective 24 May 2019. Historical reform only; current eligibility details not summarized.

sources.title: Central Bank: Announcement of new NT$1,000 and NT$500 notes, 18 July 2005
sources.note: Direct original Chinese announcement. Issued 20 July 2005, section 1(a)(5)(1) explicitly transcribes 壹仟圓 next to 1000; schoolchildren, Mikado pheasant and Yushan design; section 2 security devices. Writing is verified through issuer’s transcription, not an independently inspected banknote photograph.

proposedOverrides.name: Taiwan
proposedOverrides.summary: Taiwan’s modern self-government, authoritarian past and democratic development, with disputed status and atlas limits made explicit.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Distinct exact missing modern record; no shared association with Taiwan 1492 to 1530, China or Japanese imperial cards.
batchIdentityNotes.map: 1945 to present index; snapshots 1945, 1960, 1994, 2000 and 2010. Coarse main-island outlines omit Penghu, Kinmen, Matsu, Green Island and Orchid Island, and the 1994 outline misses tested Hualien.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Traditional Chinese 壹仟圓 explicitly transcribed by issuer in 18 July 2005 announcement for 20 July issue. Mandarin pinyin reading and denomination translation; not claimed as visual inspection of original banknote.
batchIdentityNotes.sourceLimits: Research cutoff 23 September 2026. Official CRS HTML accessible is dated August 2025; current officeholders, military movements, ally counts and projected 2026 elections are deliberately not asserted. Policy implementation and local cultural examples retain scope. Final period exclusive end 2027 includes current research year without predicting an ending.
